playlists.title: Quant HM Interview Prep
playlists.tagline: Full options-MM loop — OA → fit → concepts → data report → HM
playlists.description: From online math OA through recruiter fit, stuck-narration, onsite game theory, concise data-exercise reports, and HM behavioral rounds — what options market makers and systematic funds hire on.

episodes.title: Online math OA
episodes.problemYouSolve: Clear expectation/distribution MCQs under time pressure
sampleQuestions: E[rolls until six] and variance?
Urn draws without replacement — conditional probs?
Eigenvalues of a small matrix — diagonalizable?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: Model → derive → sanity-check → pick. Dice/balls/cards + calc + lin alg. Don't MCQ-guess without a model.
episodes.coachTip: OA is the volume filter after a harsh CV screen — treat it like a race with clean handwriting of math.

episodes.title: Recruiter fit (East Coast)
episodes.problemYouSolve: Pass location + motivation without sounding scripted
sampleQuestions: Where do you live / work?
Open to East Coast trading hubs?
Why trading vs academia or big tech?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: Honest logistics → East Coast collaboration story → one concrete day-to-day signal (quoting, valuation, live urgency).
episodes.coachTip: They are checking fit and logistics — keep it short and true.

episodes.title: Probability from first principles
episodes.problemYouSolve: Show you derive claims — not quote formulas
sampleQuestions: Expected rolls until a six — derive it.
Conditional expectation puzzle under follow-up.
When do you distrust Monte Carlo?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: Define random variable → compute expectation step-by-step → sanity-check with simulation → state variance of estimator.
episodes.coachTip: They care whether you think clearly when stuck — talk through structure.

episodes.title: Quant phone: get unstuck
episodes.problemYouSolve: Narrate depth when the path isn't obvious
sampleQuestions: Bayes with fair vs biased coin — mid-problem freeze.
Explain the concept in more depth.
What would you try next if stuck?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: State knowns → smaller case → write likelihoods explicitly → ask one precise clarifier → finish with sanity check.
episodes.coachTip: Interviewers score the stuck protocol as hard as the answer.

episodes.title: Onsite open-ended + game theory
episodes.problemYouSolve: Invent a winning theory under time pressure
sampleQuestions: Numbers summing to 15 — winning strategy?
Break down a complicated P&S question live.
How does the theory change if the target shifts?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: Define payoffs/info/strategies → map or casework → bound or compute → state residual uncertainty.
episodes.coachTip: Onsite is thinking on the fly — partial correct structure beats a lucky final number.

episodes.title: Data exercise report craft
episodes.problemYouSolve: Present trading-data findings with brutal brevity
sampleQuestions: Which 5 figures earn a slot?
Why doesn't your analysis see adverse selection?
One novel insight for a math PhD fly-out?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: Hypotheses → ≤5 decisive views → results-first summary → named failure modes. Never 200 graphs.
episodes.coachTip: Brevity is the product. If removing a plot doesn't hurt the claim, delete it.

episodes.title: Research hygiene
episodes.problemYouSolve: Prove you won't ship look-ahead bias into production
sampleQuestions: Walk me through auditing a backtest for look-ahead bias.
What failure modes do you check before trusting Sharpe 2?
How do you design point-in-time feature pipelines?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: Hypotheses → data lineage → as-of joins → train/test honesty → paper-trading gates. Name specific red flags (survivorship, corporate actions, snooping).
episodes.coachTip: Prop-shop interviewers push on *process*, not gotcha math.

episodes.title: Backtest → live production
episodes.problemYouSolve: Answer 'will this work at size?' not just 'did it backtest?'
sampleQuestions: Signal works at $10M — how do you scale to $500M?
Live PnL diverges from backtest — first hour checklist?
What makes you kill a strategy after launch?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: Capacity model → cost/impact → crowding → monitoring → pre-defined kill rules. Separate bug from alpha decay.
episodes.coachTip: Ex-prop / systematic HMs often owned PnL — speak their language on risk.

episodes.title: Tech interview basics
episodes.problemYouSolve: Still clear basic programming under a clock
sampleQuestions: Rolling mean with correct edge handling?
Complexity and NaN policy?
Vectorize a slow research loop?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: Correct code → convention for edges → O(·) → one nasty case. AI tools don't replace this round.
episodes.coachTip: Keep a small set of warm-up drills cold — rolling stats, parsing, simple simulations.

episodes.title: HM behavioral: intellectual honesty
episodes.problemYouSolve: Pass the 'would I trust this person with capital?' filter
sampleQuestions: Tell me about a time you were wrong in research.
Disagreement with a senior researcher — how did it play out?
What questions do you have for me about how we evaluate researchers?
episodes.strongAnswerFramework: STAR with a real mistake → what metric broke → process fix left behind. Questions show you evaluate *their* research culture.
episodes.coachTip: At HM stage they already like your skills — they're buying judgment and temperament.
